correctness.rationale: From B=(1-gamma)I+gamma 11^T, the eigenvalue in the all-goods direction is 1+(n-1)gamma. The branch 2+(n-1)gamma<0 forces this eigenvalue below -1. Along q=t1, the quadratic coefficient in W(q;p) is -n[1+(n-1)gamma]/2>0, hence W tends to +infinity for any finite alpha and p. This proves the incompatibility for every n in the branch; it is not inferred from the finite witness.

The conclusion assumes the unconstrained quasi-linear consumer problem implicit in the source’s inverse-demand first-order conditions. The accessible text does not specify a finite income cap; if a finite budget or nonnegative-numeraire cap was intended, that different constrained problem needs separate analysis. If linear inverse demand is instead taken as primitive, the formal dynamics remain meaningful.

value.rationale: For n>=4, the strict branch 2+(n-1)gamma<0 is nonempty under |gamma|<1 but incompatible with global maximization in the unconstrained quasi-linear problem implicit in the source’s inverse-demand first-order conditions. Removing this branch changes the economic interpretation of a whole region of the paper’s complement-side equilibrium/stability discussion; this is not a small numerical refinement.
